events.description: Al-Qaeda released a Zawahiri video on the 9/11 anniversary. It rebuts an Al Jazeera documentary and claims al-Qaeda is no client of any government. It is part of a new series called 'deal of the century / crusade of a century'. It also takes a swipe at Baghdadi and discusses the 2013 general guidelines for jihad.
English translation of the third issue of the al-Qaeda magazine One Ummah released. Its Arabic edition came out in late 2019.
Zawahiri released a lengthy 9/11 anniversary message rebutting Islamic critics of the hijackings and calling for fatwas against US military targets.
Al Jazeera aired a documentary alleging that al-Qaeda operatives were hired by Bahrain and that Abu Zubaydah had Saudi royal contacts.
Abu Zubaydah was captured.
Zawahiri was temporarily detained by the Russians in the mid-1990s.
The hosts say, citing bin Laden's files, that AQIM cut a deal with the government of Mauritania.
AQAP took over large areas of southern and central Yemen (2011-12, and again 2015-16).
Al-Qaeda circulated its general guidelines of jihad to branches, including the Islamic State of Iraq. Baghdadi never responded, which led to a split.
The Taliban admitted Mullah Omar had been dead for about two years. Zawahiri began producing material regularly from about August 2015.
AQIS was stood up.
Christopher Miller published a Washington Post op-ed arguing the war on al-Qaeda is well in sight of its end.
John Brennan declared al-Qaeda on the verge of defeat (2011-12).
A coup occurred in Mali (described as recent).
Premise of the US-Taliban deal is a US withdrawal from Afghanistan by April 2021.
US raid on bin Laden's compound yielded an archive showing he was still managing al-Qaeda.
US killed Nasser al-Wuhayshi, AQAP emir and al-Qaeda general manager (hosts say 2015 or 2016).
Joint Afghan-US raid in Helmand killed AQIS emir Asim Umar and a courier who reported directly to Zawahiri.
Mohammed Alshamrani killed three Americans at NAS Pensacola, in contact with AQAP handlers.
AQIM emir Abdelmalek Droukdel was killed.
DoD Inspector General report (dated 14 Aug, released 18 Aug) says al-Qaeda continues to fight alongside the Taliban against the Afghan government.
Christopher Miller started as NCTC director (mid-August 2020).
Miller's Washington Post op-ed claims al-Qaeda is in crisis and on the verge of collapse, calling Zawahiri its 'sole remaining ideological leader'.
US-Taliban deal for US withdrawal, criticised by the hosts as absolving the Taliban of sheltering al-Qaeda.

key_claims: Zawahiri's 2020 9/11 anniversary video was defensive and unrelated to 9/11, and was probably meant to repair al-Qaeda's brand after an Al Jazeera documentary.
Al-Qaeda is not a client or proxy of any state, but it cuts deals with states such as Mauritania, Iran and Pakistan, and the Mauritania deal shows its strength.
Al-Qaeda has a facilitation network in Iran tolerated by the Iranian government, despite tensions in Syria and Yemen, and has not declared war on Iran.
Al-Qaeda's 2013 circulation of its general guidelines to all branches, including Baghdadi's Islamic State of Iraq, shows senior leadership kept a cohesive network with its regional branches.
Al-Qaeda has expanded since 9/11, with AQAP, AQIM, al-Shabaab, AQIS and Syrian actors, so 'remnants' is the wrong description and Miller's op-ed fails to explain how the war ends.
The US has not stood up capable local allies against jihadists in Afghanistan, Yemen, Somalia, Mali, Syria, Iraq or Pakistan, and the Yemen model failed.
A US withdrawal from Afghanistan by April 2021 would likely leave the Afghan government in trouble and the Taliban, closely tied to al-Qaeda, taking large areas.
Al-Qaeda continues to fight alongside the Taliban in Afghanistan, so the US has not destroyed its Afghan safe havens.
The bin Laden files show al-Qaeda's command and control was never wrecked and that bin Laden was still managing al-Qaeda globally in 2011.
Zawahiri is an operational emir who directs regional branches and has been in charge of AQIM and communicates through couriers, not merely an 'ideological leader'.
Zawahiri is not the 'sole remaining leader': Saif al-Adel and Abu Muhammad al-Masri are in Iran, and a new generation such as Hamza al-Khalidi exists, with a succession plan in place.
The September 2019 Helmand raid showed Asim Umar of AQIS had a courier reporting directly to Zawahiri.
The Pensacola attacker was directed by AQAP handlers, showing that al-Qaeda retains the ability to direct external attacks.
Al-Qaeda's insurgencies are its lifeblood and are not defeated in any theater; US allies in Afghanistan, Somalia, Yemen and Mali are the ones struggling to survive.
The US-Taliban deal and US withdrawals absolve the Taliban of sheltering al-Qaeda, and the jihadists draw the conclusion that they outlasted the US.
